Unit 1 • HL

Advanced Architecture

Introduction

Why do we need different chips for different jobs?

This HL unit explores Specialisation and Concurrency. You will move beyond the basic CPU to understand why modern computing relies on Massive Parallelism (GPUs) and Pipelining to handle complex tasks like AI and 3D rendering. You will also dive into how high-level code is translated into machine code via Interpreters, Compilers, and Virtual Machines.

You'll begin by comparing the diverse skillset of the CPU vs the raw power of the GPU. Then you'll optimize execution using Pipelining and investigate the abstraction layers of Bytecode and JIT Compilation.

CPU vs GPU Architecture

Different tools for different jobs:

  • CPU (Swiss Army Knife): Few powerful cores, Complex control, Low latency. Good for sequential logic (OS, Apps).
  • GPU (Chainsaw): Thousands of weak cores, High throughput. Good for parallel data (Graphics, AI, Mining).

Pipelining

How to make a slow processor feel fast. Pipelining overlaps instructions:

  • Sequential: Fetch 1 -> Decode 1 -> Execute 1 -> Fetch 2...
  • Pipelined: Fetch 3 | Decode 2 | Execute 1 (All happening at once).
  • Implication: Increases Throughput (tasks per second), not individual speed.

Translation: Compilers vs Interpreters

Computers only speak binary. How do we get there?

  • Compiler: Translate Everything at once -> Run later. (Fast execution, Slow dev).
  • Interpreter: Translate Line-by-Line -> Run immediately. (Slow execution, Fast dev).

Virtual Machines & JIT

The best of both worlds? Java and Python use Bytecode.

  • Virtual Machine: Software CPU that runs Bytecode anywhere (Portability).
  • JIT (Just-In-Time): The VM compiles hot code to machine code while running for speed.

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
ParallelismDoing multiple things at exactly the same time (e.g., GPU cores working on different pixels).
ConcurrencyDealing with multiple things at once (e.g., Pipelining features of a single core).
ThroughputThe amount of work performed by a system in a given time.
LatencyThe time it takes to process a single instruction from start to finish.
PipeliningA technique where multiple instructions are overlapped in execution.
BytecodeIntermediate code (like a half-way translation) that usually runs on a Virtual Machine.
Virtual Machine (VM)Software that emulates hardware, allowing code to run on any physical machine.
JIT CompilationJust-In-Time. Compiling bytecode into native machine code at runtime to improve performance.

Common Misconceptions

Pipelining makes instructions faster

No! Each instruction takes the same time. But you finish MORE instructions per second because you overlap them.

GPU is better than CPU

Try running Windows on a GPU. It would crash. GPUs are terrible at complex logic/branching; they only excel at repetitive math.

Compiler = Better

Not always. Interpreters allow cross-platform portability and easier debugging. It's a trade-off.

Think Deeper

"The End of Moore's Law?" We can't make transistors much smaller. Is massive parallelism (GPUs/TPUs) the only way left to speed up computers?
